items.content:
16mm has roughly four times the negative area, so it resolves properly
and you can actually project it. 8mm is cheaper per minute and has the
grain structure everyone actually wants when they say they want film.

Stock is the real constraint either way — fewer emulsions every year, and
the processing labs are down to a handful.

summary: Compares negative area, cost and grain; stock is the real constraint
title: 8mm vs 16mm, practically
